trust_decision.summary: In _handleAddress the parser decides whether a text run is a quoted local part and, when that text becomes the address, must restore its quotes BEFORE _recoverAddrSpec peels trailing comment wreckage; at the pinned commit the quotes are put back only after the recovery, so the run that became the address was never an addr-spec the recovery could split and the whole 'user@good-corp.com evil.com' string is handed on as the envelope recipient.

landing_point.why: The summary names 'malformed envelope recipient through RFC 5322 comment parsing', so an engineer starts at the point where a parsed address is finalised and the comment-wreckage recovery runs, with the quoted-text quoting sitting just below it at 529-531.

fix_sites.entry_point: addressparser(value) (also reached by MimeNode.setHeader('To', value) -> getEnvelope())
fix_sites.module_kind: public API module, dependency-free address parser (package subpath nodemailer/lib/addressparser)

fix_sites.entry_point: addressparser(value) (also reached by MimeNode.setHeader('To', value) -> getEnvelope())

O3_reason_to_dismiss: mime-node's _normalizeAddress/_normalizeLocalPart is a second, stricter rule that only re-quotes a local part it is handed, and an object-shaped address has already been parsed, so a solver can call the envelope-side cleaning out of scope for a header-parsing bug.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A well-formed quoted local part must keep its interior whitespace, its '@' and its escaped quote instead of being split by the new recovery, and a quoted display name beside an address must stay a display name.

O6_input_shapes: quoted local part containing whitespace ('"user name"@good-corp.com(x)evil.com')
quoted local part containing an escaped quote ('"test\"quote"@example.com')
several or empty comments after the domain ('(x)(y)', '()', '(x)a(y)b')
trailing junk with no comment ('"user@evil.com"@good-corp.com junk')
leading display name or comment before the quoted local part ('Name "user"@x', '(c)"user"@x', '"Name" "user"@x')

O7_producer.where: src/addressparser/index.ts:597-601 (Tokenizer.tokenize drops empty text nodes, so an empty quoted string leaves no token of its own for textWasQuoted to be recorded on; _handleAddress only sees the token list)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Object-shaped address ({name, address}) passed to MimeNode.setHeader('To'|'Cc'|'Bcc') or setEnvelope() skips addressparser entirely and only gets _normalizeAddress, which keeps an interior comment tail or interior whitespace, so '"user"@good-corp.com(x)evil.com' still reaches envelope.to with the text after the comment attached
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The object is already parsed, so normalisation only has to clean characters and the comment tail is the caller's problem, not the parser's
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file away from the landing point, in src/mime-node, one layer above the parser

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second local-part quoting rule in the message layer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: MimeNode has to emit strict RFC 5321 dot-atoms while the parser ships dependency-free, so the maintainer duplicated the rule; the fix's own comment at src/addressparser/index.ts:72-75 says the two are kept separate on purpose

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another token-shape rule in the tokenizer that drops tokens before a quoting flag can be recorded (empty comment, empty angle-addr pair)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The tokenizer already drops empty text nodes before _handleAddress sees them, so a maintainer adding an adjacent drop rule is the same shape of bug

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Envelope-address mapping that reinterprets a bare name as an address after the parser has run
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: setEnvelope accepts a bare username such as 'root', so a rewrite of that mapping that moves or re-quotes an address is realistic and sits after the check

O9_family: Improper input validation / parser differential in address parsing (CWE-20, CWE-436)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Split the joined text on whitespace or strip the tail where the text becomes the address, which also strips the legal whitespace inside a quoted local part and breaks '"user name"@example.com' and quoted display names.
